claim: Fluc family fluoride channels protect microbes against ambient environmental fluoride by undermining the cytoplasmic accumulation of this toxic halide.
source: Fluc family fluoride channels protect microbes against ambient environmental fluoride by undermining the cytoplasmic accumulation of this toxic halide.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Baker et al., 2012; Ji et al., 2014; McIlwain et al., 2021).

claim: Fluc channels are structurally idiosyncratic, with no analogy to other known ion channels.
source: These proteins are structurally idiosyncratic, and thus the permeation pathway and mechanism have no analogy in other known ion channels.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a characterization of Fluc channels.

claim: Fluoride-binding sites were identified in previous structural studies of Fluc channels.
source: Although fluoride-binding sites were identified in previous structural studies, it was not evident how these ions access aqueous solution, and the molecular determinants of anion recognition and selectivity have not been elucidated.
evidence: This refers to prior work and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Additional binding sites along the permeation pathway were identified using x-ray crystallography, planar bilayer electrophysiology, and liposome-based assays.
source: Using x-ray crystallography, planar bilayer electrophysiology, and liposome-based assays, we identified additional binding sites along the permeation pathway.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the results section.

claim: An oriented system for planar lipid bilayer electrophysiology was developed.
source: We used this information to develop an oriented system for planar lipid bilayer electrophysiology and observed anion block at one of these sites, revealing insights into the mechanism of anion recognition.
evidence: This is a methodological development described in the abstract and demonstrated in the results.

claim: Anion block was observed at one of the binding sites, revealing insights into the mechanism of anion recognition.
source: We used this information to develop an oriented system for planar lipid bilayer electrophysiology and observed anion block at one of these sites, revealing insights into the mechanism of anion recognition.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by electrophysiology data in Figure 4.

claim: The proposed permeation mechanism involves alternating occupancy of anion-binding sites that are fully assembled only as the substrate approaches.
source: We propose a permeation mechanism involving alternating occupancy of anion-binding sites that are fully assembled only as the substrate approaches.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on the experimental findings and structural analysis.

claim: Fluc channels are small, homodimeric ion channels.
source: These small, homodimeric ion channels are remarkable proteins in two regards
evidence: This is a structural characterization supported by previous structural studies cited in the text.

claim: Fluc channels have a dual-topology architecture in which the two subunits of the homodimer are arranged antiparallel with respect to each other.
source: first, their unusual 'dual-topology' architecture, in which the two subunits of the homodimer are arranged antiparallel with respect to each other (Stockbridge et al., 2014; Stockbridge et al., 2013), yielding a double-barreled pair of pores related by twofold symmetry (Stockbridge et al., 2015; Last et al., 2016; Turman et al., 2015; Turman and Stockbridge, 2017)
evidence: This is a structural feature supported by multiple citations to previous structural studies.

claim: Fluc channels yield a double-barreled pair of pores related by twofold symmetry.
source: first, their unusual 'dual-topology' architecture, in which the two subunits of the homodimer are arranged antiparallel with respect to each other (Stockbridge et al., 2014; Stockbridge et al., 2013), yielding a double-barreled pair of pores related by twofold symmetry (Stockbridge et al., 2015; Last et al., 2016; Turman et al., 2015; Turman and Stockbridge, 2017)
evidence: This is a structural feature supported by multiple citations.

claim: Fluc channels exhibit extreme substrate selectivity with >10,000-fold selectivity against chloride.
source: second, the Flucs stand out among anion channels for their extreme substrate selectivity (Stockbridge et al., 2013). In contrast to most characterized families of anion channels, which tend to be non-selective among anions and sometimes poorly discriminate against cations, the Flucs are arguably the most selective ion channels known, with >10,000-fold selectivity against the biologically abundant chloride (Stockbridge et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a functional property supported by citation to Stockbridge et al., 2013.

claim: The extreme selectivity of Fluc channels prevents collapse of the membrane potential due to chloride or cation leak.
source: This extreme selectivity prevents collapse of the membrane potential due to chloride or cation leak through the Fluc channels, which are constitutively open.
evidence: This is a functional interpretation based on the selectivity data.

claim: Fluc channels are constitutively open.
source: This extreme selectivity prevents collapse of the membrane potential due to chloride or cation leak through the Fluc channels, which are constitutively open.
evidence: This is a functional property stated in the text.

claim: Most characterized anion channels are non-selective among anions and sometimes poorly discriminate against cations.
source: In contrast to most characterized families of anion channels, which tend to be non-selective among anions and sometimes poorly discriminate against cations, the Flucs are arguably the most selective ion channels known
evidence: This is a comparative statement about anion channels in general, based on established knowledge.

claim: Crystal structures of Fluc-Bpe and Fluc-Ec2 provide an opportunity to understand the molecular basis for anion permeation in the Flucs.
source: Crystal structures of representative Fluc channels from Bordetella pertussis (Fluc-Bpe) and an Escherichia coli virulence plasmid (Fluc-Ec2) provide an opportunity to understand the molecular basis for anion permeation in the Flucs (Stockbridge et al., 2015; McIlwain et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: Fluc channels possess two deep, aqueous vestibules with an electropositive character.
source: The protein possesses two deep, aqueous vestibules with an electropositive character due to an absolutely conserved arginine sidechain and a deeply buried sodium ion at the center of the protein (Turman and Stockbridge, 2017; McIlwain et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a structural feature supported by citations.

claim: The electropositive character of the vestibules is due to an absolutely conserved arginine sidechain and a deeply buried sodium ion.
source: The protein possesses two deep, aqueous vestibules with an electropositive character due to an absolutely conserved arginine sidechain and a deeply buried sodium ion at the center of the protein (Turman and Stockbridge, 2017; McIlwain et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a structural explanation supported by citations.

claim: Crystal structures captured four electron densities assigned as fluoride ions, two in each pore.
source: The structures captured four electron densities assigned as fluoride ions, two in each pore, positioned near the center of the protein, at some distance from the vestibules.
evidence: This is a structural observation from previous crystal structures.

claim: The fluoride ions are aligned along the polar face of TM4, referred to as the polar track.
source: These ions are aligned along the polar face of TM4, referred to as the polar track.
evidence: This is a structural description from previous studies.

claim: The fluoride ions are located 6–10 Å from the aqueous solution, with no clear aqueous pathway leading to the external solution.
source: They are located 6–10 Å from the aqueous solution, with no clear aqueous pathway leading to the external solution.
evidence: This is a structural observation that motivated the current study.

claim: Mutation of the sidechains that coordinate the proposed fluoride ions inhibits fluoride throughput but does not alter the ion selectivity.
source: Mutation of the sidechains that coordinate the proposed fluoride ions inhibits fluoride throughput but does not alter the ion selectivity of these proteins (Stockbridge et al., 2015; Last et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a functional observation from previous mutagenesis studies.

claim: The structure of Fluc-Ec2 in the presence of 100 mM Br- was solved.
source: We were unable to generate diffracting Fluc-Bpe crystals in the presence of Br-, but we were successful in solving the structure of Fluc-Ec2 in the presence of 100 mM Br- (Table 1).
evidence: This is a primary experimental result of the study, supported by crystallographic data in Table 1.

claim: Anomalous difference maps show two prominent peaks located in equivalent, non-crystallographic symmetry-related positions at the bottom of the aqueous vestibules.
source: Anomalous difference maps show two prominent peaks, located in equivalent, non-crystallographic symmetry-related positions at the bottom of the aqueous vestibules (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the Br- crystal structure, shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The bromide densities are coordinated by Ser81 and Thr82 in Fluc-Ec2.
source: These densities are coordinated by a sidechain that is invariant among Fluc channels, Ser81, along with the highly conserved Thr82 (Figure 1B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ser81 is invariant among Fluc channels.
source: These densities are coordinated by a sidechain that is invariant among Fluc channels, Ser81, along with the highly conserved Thr82 (Figure 1B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a sequence conservation observation.

claim: Thr82 is highly conserved in Fluc channels.
source: These densities are coordinated by a sidechain that is invariant among Fluc channels, Ser81, along with the highly conserved Thr82 (Figure 1B, upper panel).
evidence: This is a sequence conservation observation.

claim: A positive density occupies the same position in previous Fluc-Bpe structures.
source: In maps from previous Fluc-Bpe structures (Stockbridge et al., 2015), a positive density occupies this same position between the homologous hydroxyl sidechains (Figure 1B, lower panel).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous structural data, shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The bromide-binding site is exposed to bulk water in the vestibule but is likely to be partially dehydrated.
source: This site is exposed to bulk water in the vestibule but is likely to be partially dehydrated, with aliphatic sidechains, including Ile48 in close proximity to the bound bromide ion (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a structural interpretation based on the crystal structure, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ile48 is in close proximity to the bound bromide ion.
source: This site is exposed to bulk water in the vestibule but is likely to be partially dehydrated, with aliphatic sidechains, including Ile48 in close proximity to the bound bromide ion (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from Figure 1C.

claim: MTSES modification of I48C in Fluc-Ec2 reduces fluoride currents by ~50%.
source: In planar lipid bilayers, I48C mediates robust fluoride currents, which rapidly diminish by ~50% upon addition of saturating MTSES to the cis chamber (Figure 1D), consistent with full modification of a cis-facing thiol in a population of channels with oppositely oriented pores.
evidence: This is an experimental result from electrophysiology, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: MTSES addition to wild-type Fluc-Ec2 (C74A background) does not alter fluoride currents.
source: In contrast, MTSES addition to channels with WT I48 (C74A background) does not alter the fluoride currents (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a control experiment shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Mutation of Ile50 in Fluc-Bpe to tryptophan diminished the rate of fluoride transport by ~400-fold.
source: However, mutation of Ile50 in Bpe to a bulkier tryptophan sidechain diminished the rate of fluoride transport by ~400-fold in liposome efflux experiments, possibly by sterically hindering fluoride access to the bottom of the vestibule (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from liposome flux assays, shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: S81A mutation in Fluc-Ec2 resulted in a ~50% decrease in conductance to 3.7 ± 0.4 pS.
source: S81A had a mild effect, with a ~50% decrease in conductance to 3.7 ± 0.4 pS (seven single-channel measurements), compared to 7 pS for the WT protein (Stockbridge et al., 2013; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Wild-type Fluc-Ec2 has a conductance of 7 pS.
source: S81A had a mild effect, with a ~50% decrease in conductance to 3.7 ± 0.4 pS (seven single-channel measurements), compared to 7 pS for the WT protein (Stockbridge et al., 2013; Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a reference to previous measurements.

claim: S81A/T82A double mutant had fluoride throughput diminished to 8530 ± 30 s−1, a ~100-fold reduction in the rate.
source: The S81A/T82A double mutant had a more severe effect, with fluoride throughput diminished to 8530 ± 30 s−1, a ~100-fold reduction in the rate (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental result from liposome flux assays, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A strong anomalous peak persisted in the S81A structure.
source: In accord with the fluoride transport experiments, a strong anomalous peak persisted in the S81A structure but was weaker in the S81A/T82A double mutant (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The anomalous peak was weaker in the S81A/T82A double mutant.
source: In accord with the fluoride transport experiments, a strong anomalous peak persisted in the S81A structure but was weaker in the S81A/T82A double mutant (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In S81A and S81A/T82A mutants, the bromide densities shifted away from the channel center toward the external solution, moving about 2 Å closer to the vestibule Arg22s.
source: In both cases, the densities shifted away from the channel center toward the external solution, moving about 2 Å closer to the vestibule Arg22s.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures.

claim: S81C and S81T mutants had completely abolished fluoride efflux from liposomes.
source: The S81C and S81T phenotypes were more extreme: for both mutants, fluoride efflux from liposomes was completely abolished (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an experimental result from liposome flux assays, shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In the S81C structure, an anomalous density is present in the vestibule but has moved ~2 Å farther up into the aqueous vestibule, relative to the Br- position in the WT protein.
source: An anomalous density is present in the vestibule, but has moved ~2 Å farther up into the aqueous vestibule, relative to the Br- position in the WT protein (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the S81C crystal structure, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The electropositive environment of the vestibule may perturb the cysteine pKa in S81C such that it is deprotonated at pH 7.5.
source: We posit that the electropositive environment of the vestibule perturbs the cysteine pKa such that it is deprotonated at the pH of these experiments (pH 9 in the crystal structure and pH 7.5 in the liposome flux experiments).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation based on structural and functional data.

claim: PropKa calculates an approximate pKa value of 6 for S81C in the crystal structure.
source: The pKa prediction software PropKa reinforces this possibility, calculating an approximate pKa value of 6 for S81C in the crystal structure of this mutant (Bas et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a computational prediction cited from Bas et al., 2008.

claim: Fluoride currents mediated by Ec2 S81C increased dramatically when the pH was decreased from 7.4 to 5.5.
source: Whereas fluoride currents were near zero at pH 7.4, currents increased dramatically when the pH was decreased to 5.5 (Figure 2E, Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental result from electrophysiology, shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: The increase in F- currents for S81C was fully reversible with pH.
source: The increase in F- currents was fully reversible with pH, and WT activity was not altered by changing pH over this range.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the pH titration experiments.

claim: Wild-type Fluc activity was not altered by changing pH from 5.5 to 7.4.
source: The increase in F- currents was fully reversible with pH, and WT activity was not altered by changing pH over this range.
evidence: This is a control experiment.

claim: Fluc-Bpe S83C exhibits similar pH sensitivity to Fluc-Ec2 S81C.
source: The analogous mutation in Fluc-Bpe channels, S83C, exhibits similar pH sensitivity (Figure 2E, Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental result shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: The anion-binding site at the bottom of the vestibule is on the fluoride permeation pathway.
source: Taken together, these experiments show that the anion-binding site at the bottom of the vestibule is on the fluoride permeation pathway .
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutagenesis and structural data.

claim: The anion-binding site is located immediately adjacent to one of the fluoride ions in the polar track.
source: This anion-binding site is located immediately adjacent to one of the fluoride ions in the polar track, and we imagine fluoride ions enter the vestibule, become dehydrated, before eventually being stripped of water entirely as the ion is translocated from the bottom of the vestibule to the polar track.
evidence: This is a structural observation and mechanistic interpretation.

claim: Translocation between the vestibule and the polar track must contribute to anion selectivity since the bromide anomalous density is observed in the vestibule but never in the polar track.
source: Translocation between the vestibule and the polar track must contribute to anion selectivity since the bromide anomalous density is observed in the former location, but never in the latter.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data showing Br- in the vestibule but not the polar track.

claim: No change in chloride transport was detected for the vestibule mutants.
source: However, we could not detect any change in chloride transport by these mutants (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), motivating us to search for additional pore-lining sidechains on the opposite end of the pore.
evidence: This is an experimental result from chloride flux assays, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In eukaryotic FEX proteins, residues that line one pore are highly conserved, whereas the corresponding residues from the second, vestigial pore have drifted.
source: In the FEX proteins, this ancient fusion event has permitted drift of redundant sequences, including degradation of one of the two pores (Berbasova et al., 2017). A clear pattern has been identified in which residues that line one pore (mostly, but not entirely, from the C-terminal domain) are highly conserved, whereas the corresponding residues from the second, vestigial pore (mostly, but not entirely, from the N-terminal domain) have drifted (Stockbridge et al., 2015; Smith et al., 2015; Berbasova et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a sequence conservation pattern supported by multiple citations.

claim: Three additional residues (a threonine, a tyrosine, and a glutamate) follow the same pattern of conservation as other pore-lining sequences in eukaryotic FEX proteins.
source: We identified three additional residues that follow the same pattern of conservation as other pore-lining sequences: a threonine, a tyrosine, and a glutamate (blue highlighting in alignment).
evidence: This is a sequence analysis result shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the Fluc-Bpe structure, Thr39, Glu88, and Tyr104 associate within hydrogen-bonding distance of each other.
source: In the Fluc-Bpe structure, the three homologous sidechains (Thr39, Glu88, and Tyr104) associate within hydrogen-bonding distance of each other, one contributed by each pore-lining helix, TM2, TM3, and TM4.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the Fluc-Bpe structure.

claim: Thr39, Glu88, and Tyr104 are positioned near the protein's aqueous vestibules.
source: They are positioned near the protein's aqueous vestibules, and Tyr104 is also within hydrogen-bonding distance of a fluoride ion within the pore (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Tyr104 is within hydrogen-bonding distance of a fluoride ion within the pore.
source: They are positioned near the protein's aqueous vestibules, and Tyr104 is also within hydrogen-bonding distance of a fluoride ion within the pore (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a structural observation shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Thr39 is conserved in ~95% of Fluc sequences.
source: From an alignment of all homodimeric Fluc sequences in the PFAM database (Mistry et al., 2021), we found that Thr39 is conserved in ~95% of the sequences we studied
evidence: This is a sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Glu88 is conserved in >85% of Fluc sequences (~10% Asp and ~ 5% Gln).
source: Glu88 is conserved in >85% of sequences (~10% Asp and ~ 5% Gln)
evidence: This is a sequence conservation analysis.

claim: Tyr104 is conserved in 55% of Fluc sequences (~35% Asn and ~15% Ser).
source: Tyr104 is conserved in 55% of sequences (~35% Asn and ~15% Ser).
evidence: This is a sequence conservation analysis.

claim: T39S retained F- conductance to at least 75% of WT levels.
source: T39S, E88D, and Y104F retained F- conductance to at least 75% of WT levels, and we do not interpret these differences as mechanistically important.
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology shown in Figure 3C.

claim: E88D retained F- conductance to at least 75% of WT levels.
source: T39S, E88D, and Y104F retained F- conductance to at least 75% of WT levels, and we do not interpret these differences as mechanistically important.
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Y104F retained F- conductance to at least 75% of WT levels.
source: T39S, E88D, and Y104F retained F- conductance to at least 75% of WT levels, and we do not interpret these differences as mechanistically important.
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology shown in Figure 3C.

claim: E88Q exhibited currents one-fifth of the WT levels.
source: In contrast, E88Q exhibited currents one-fifth of the WT levels, a more substantial difference that is also statistically significant at p<0.0001 (unpaired t-test).
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology shown in Figure 3C.

claim: T39S undergoes long periods of robust throughput (τo = 9.2 ± 0.2 s), punctuated by brief channel closures (τc = 35.3 ± 0.4 ms).
source: T39S undergoes long periods of robust throughput (τo = 9.2 ± 0.2 s), punctuated by brief channel closures (τc = 35.3 ± 0.4 ms) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Y104F had shorter open intervals (τo = 1.9 ± 0.2 s and τc = 33.2 ± 2.5 ms).
source: Y104F was more dynamic, with shorter open intervals (τo = 1.9 ± 0.2 s and τc = 33.2 ± 2.5 ms) (Figure 3D, inset).
evidence: This is an experimental result from single-channel electrophysiology shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Wild-type Fluc-Bpe proteins are constitutively open and show no closures or sub-conductance states.
source: T39S and Y104F both showed differences in dynamic behavior compared to WT Fluc-Bpe proteins, which are constitutively open and show no closures or sub-conductance states.
evidence: This is a characterization of wild-type behavior.

claim: One role of the triad is to stabilize the three pore-lining helices in an open, fluoride-conducting conformation.
source: Thus, single-channel recordings suggest that one role of the triad is to stabilize the three pore-lining helices in an open, fluoride-conducting conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the gating behavior of the mutants.

claim: None of the fluoride-conductive mutants constructed thus far transport chloride ion.
source: None of the fluoride-conductive mutants constructed thus far transport chloride ion, as probed using our most sensitive metric of chloride transport, liposome efflux assays (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental result from chloride flux assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Halides and pseudohalides inhibit fluoride currents with a wide range of potencies.
source: However, we noticed that halides and pseudohalides inhibit fluoride currents with a wide range of potencies (Figure 4A, Table 2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from anion block experiments shown in Figure 4A and Table 2.

claim: The recognition series for anion block is OCN->SCN->NO3->Cl-.
source: The recognition series (OCN->SCN->NO3->Cl-) deviates from common determinants of anion selectivity, such as anion radius, ΔGhydration, ΔGBorn, or the lyotropic (Hofmeister) series (Table 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the anion block experiments.

claim: The inhibitory effects of anions are best fit by a two-site-binding isotherm, with weak binding to a second site.
source: The inhibitory effects are best fit by a two-site-binding isotherm, with weak binding to a second site (Table 2).
evidence: This is a data analysis result shown in Table 2.

claim: The S83C vestibule mutant was used to create an oriented system for electrophysiology by recording channels under asymmetric pH conditions.
source: In order to separate the effects of anion block at these two positions, and to better quantify the affinity, we exploited the S83C vestibule mutant described in Figure 2E by recording channels under asymmetric pH conditions. The cis side of the bilayer was maintained at pH 7.5, silencing any pore with a cis-facing vestibular S83C. The trans side of the bilayer was adjusted to pH 5.5, so that pores with a trans-facing vestibular S83C retained WT-like function (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a methodological approach described in the text and illustrated in Figure 4B.

claim: OCN- blocks fluoride currents almost to the zero-current level at 30 mM in the oriented system.
source: In OCN- titration experiments, currents were reduced almost to the zero-current level at 30 mM OCN-, showing that the higher affinity OCN--binding site is on the triad side of the pore (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an experimental result from the oriented system shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The higher affinity OCN--binding site is on the triad side of the pore.
source: In OCN- titration experiments, currents were reduced almost to the zero-current level at 30 mM OCN-, showing that the higher affinity OCN--binding site is on the triad side of the pore (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the oriented system experiments shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The apparent affinity of OCN- increased as F- concentration decreased, showing that binding and inhibition at the triad site is competitive with fluoride.
source: Using the oriented system, we performed OCN- addition experiments in the presence of 30–300 mM F-. The apparent affinity of OCN- increased as F- concentration decreased, showing that binding and inhibition at the triad site is competitive with fluoride (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an experimental result from Lineweaver-Burke analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: For both OCN- and Cl-, block of the fluoride currents in the oriented system was well approximated by a single-site-binding isotherm that saturates at full inhibition.
source: For both OCN- and Cl-, block of the fluoride currents was well approximated by a single-site-binding isotherm that saturates at full inhibition, although we did not perform experiments at the ~molar Cl- concentrations that would be required to fully block currents (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Table 2).
evidence: This is a data analysis result shown in Figure 4E and Table 2.

claim: Under experimental conditions with 300 mM F-, the Ki value for chloride is ~400 mM in the oriented system.
source: Under our usual experimental conditions with 300 mM F-, a fit to a single-site-binding isotherm yielded Ki values of ~400 mM for chloride, the most abundant biological halide, and 8 mM for OCN-, in very good agreement with the value estimated from the dual-topology WT channels (Table 2).
evidence: This is a data analysis result shown in Table 2.

claim: Under experimental conditions with 300 mM F-, the Ki value for OCN- is 8 mM in the oriented system.
source: Under our usual experimental conditions with 300 mM F-, a fit to a single-site-binding isotherm yielded Ki values of ~400 mM for chloride, the most abundant biological halide, and 8 mM for OCN-, in very good agreement with the value estimated from the dual-topology WT channels (Table 2).
evidence: This is a data analysis result shown in Table 2.

claim: OCN- is not permeant through Fluc-Bpe channels.
source: Although OCN- blocked Fluc-Bpe with relatively high affinity, liposome flux experiments showed that OCN- is not permeant (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an experimental result from liposome flux assays shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The appreciable ~60-fold difference in Cl- and OCN- block characteristic of WT channels is almost eliminated for E88Q channels, which display only ~fourfold difference in Cl- and OCN- affinity.
source: The appreciable ~60-fold difference in Cl- and OCN- block characteristic of WT channels is almost eliminated for E88Q channels, which display only ~fourfold difference in Cl- and OCN- affinity (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 5, Table 2).
evidence: This is an experimental result from anion block experiments on E88Q shown in Figure 4F and Table 2.

claim: The effect of E88Q on anion block is almost entirely due to the 10-fold less potent block of E88Q by OCN-.
source: This effect is almost entirely due to the 10-fold less potent block of E88Q by OCN-.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data in Figure 4F and Table 2.

claim: Glu88 contributes to anion recognition at the end of the pore defined by the T-E-Y triad.
source: Even if we are cautious in quantifying the effect because Cl- block cannot be measured to saturation, a qualitative reading of these experiments suggests that Glu88 contributes to anion recognition at the end of the pore defined by the T-E-Y triad.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the E88Q anion block experiments.

claim: Ion accumulation in aqueous entryways is a well-characterized feature of many ion channels, serving to increase the rate at which ions process to the constricted selectivity filter.
source: Ion accumulation in aqueous entryways is a well-characterized feature of many ion channels, serving to increase the rate at which ions process to the constricted selectivity filter (Doyle et al., 1998; Latorre and Miller, 1983; Payandeh et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a general principle of ion channel function supported by citations.

claim: The vestibule serine (S81 in Fluc-Ec2/S83 in Fluc-Bpe) is absolutely invariant in Fluc channels.
source: We speculate that the vestibule serine (S81 in Fluc-Ec2/S83 in Fluc-Bpe), which is absolutely invariant in Fluc channels, plays a central role in fluoride access to the dehydrated polar track.
evidence: This is a statement about sequence conservation.

claim: A rotamerization of the vestibule serine would bring this sidechain within hydrogen-bonding distance of the F1 fluoride position.
source: It is worth noting that a rotamerization of the vestibule serine would bring this sidechain within hydrogen-bonding distance of one such polar track fluoride position, F1 (Figure 5, right panel).
evidence: This is a structural observation and mechanistic speculation shown in Figure 5.

claim: A mechanism involving translocation of fluoride ions by rotamerization of amino acid sidechains lining the pore has been proposed for the Fluc channels previously.
source: A mechanism involving translocation of fluoride ions by rotamerization of amino acid sidechains lining the pore has been proposed for the Fluc channels previously and would be consistent with the measured conductance of these proteins (Stockbridge et al., 2015; Last et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a reference to previous mechanistic proposals.

claim: Threonine enjoys less conformational flexibility than serine.
source: Since threonine enjoys less conformational flexibility than serine, such a mechanism might explain why S81T is non-functional in Fluc-Ec2 and why the Ser to Thr substitution has not arisen over evolutionary time in any Fluc channel.
evidence: This is a chemical property of amino acids used to explain the functional data.

claim: The hydrogen bond between the fluoride and the vestibule serine seems to be dispensable, and mutant channels with an alanine at the position retain robust fluoride currents.
source: The hydrogen bond between the fluoride and the vestibule serine seems to be dispensable, and mutant channels with an alanine at the position retain robust fluoride currents.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the S81A/S83A functional data.

claim: Conversion of polar track residues to alanine had mild consequences for Fluc-Ec2.
source: Similarly, conversion of polar track residues to alanine also had mild consequences for Fluc-Ec2 (Last et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a reference to previous mutagenesis studies.

claim: In the resting state of the channel, the E88 carboxylate resides in the position observed in the crystal structures.
source: We propose that, in the resting state of the channel, the E88 carboxylate resides in the position observed in the crystal structures (Figure 5, right panel) (in structures, this position is additionally enforced by monobody binding).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on structural data shown in Figure 5.

claim: E88 is stabilized in its resting position by the positive dipole of helix 3b and hydrogen bond donors T39 and Y104.
source: E88 is stabilized in this position by the positive dipole of helix 3b and hydrogen bond donors T39 and Y104, where it helps compensate the otherwise positive electrostatics of the unoccupied channel.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on structural features.

claim: When F- is present, the permeant anion electrostatically repels the E88 carboxylate, perhaps competing for the same binding site at the top of helix 3b.
source: We suggest that when F- is present, the permeant anion electrostatically repels the E88 carboxylate, perhaps competing for the same binding site at the top of helix 3b (Figure 5, left panel).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal shown in Figure 5.

claim: For a series of halides and pseudohalides, the selectivity series is correlated to the pKa of the conjugate acid.
source: We observed that, for a series of halides and pseudohalides, the selectivity series is correlated to the pKa of the conjugate acid (Table 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is an observation from the anion block data shown in Table 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: pKa is a proxy for the anion's strength as a hydrogen bond acceptor (basicity).
source: we propose that pKa is actually a proxy for the anion's strength as a hydrogen bond acceptor (basicity).
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the correlation between pKa and anion block.

claim: pKa and basicity are relatively well correlated within a single anionic series, such as the halide/pseudohalide series.
source: Although pKa and basicity are not strictly correlated across anion types, the properties are relatively well correlated within a single anionic series, such as the halide/pseudohalide series tested here (Pike et al., 2017; Gilli et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a chemical principle supported by citations.

claim: An anion's propensity to serve as a hydrogen bond acceptor contributes to its recognition by the Flucs.
source: Thus, we suggest that an anion's propensity to serve as a hydrogen bond acceptor contributes to its recognition by the Flucs, helping to explain the channel's remarkable indifference to Cl-, the fluoride ion's most biologically relevant competitor.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on the anion block data and chemical properties.

claim: F- is a strong hydrogen bond acceptor.
source: In contrast to Cl-, and like OCN-, F- is a famously strong hydrogen bond acceptor.
evidence: This is a chemical property of fluoride.

claim: The negative charge of the fluoride ions is counterbalanced by the protein's few positive charges, the vestibule arginines and the structural central Na+.
source: The negative charge of the fluoride ions is counterbalanced by the protein's few positive charges, the vestibule arginines and the structural central Na+.
evidence: This is a structural and electrostatic principle of the proposed mechanism.

claim: Both pores of Fluc channels are functional for F- permeation.
source: Experiments have shown that both pores are functional for F- permeation (Last et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a reference to previous experimental work.

claim: It is highly unlikely that all six anion positions (three anions in each of two pores) are simultaneously occupied.
source: but it seems highly unlikely that all six anion positions (three anions in each of two pores) are simultaneously occupied.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on electrostatic considerations.

claim: A scenario of alternating occupancy is proposed, in which a fluoride moving into one binding site electrostatically hastens its neighbor into the next position in the sequence.
source: Rather, we imagine a scenario of alternating occupancy, as proposed for other multi-ion pores, in which a fluoride moving into one binding site electrostatically hastens its neighbor into the next position in the sequence.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on principles from other ion channels.

claim: The densities observed in the crystal structure may represent partially occupied fluoride sites or the monobodies used as crystallization chaperones may alter the electrostatic landscape in the pore, increasing ion occupancy.
source: We propose either that the densities observed in the crystal structure represent partially occupied fluoride sites or that the monobodies used as crystallization chaperones alter the electrostatic landscape in the pore, increasing ion occupancy.
evidence: This is a speculation about the interpretation of the crystal structures.

claim: In crystal structures of Fluc-Bpe with a monobody occupying only one side of the channel, each pore contained only one fluoride density, rather than two, in the polar track.
source: Indeed, in crystal structures of Fluc-Bpe with a monobody occupying only one side of the channel, each pore contained only one fluoride density, rather than two, in the polar track (McIlwain et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a structural observation from a previous study.

claim: As additional fluoride ions enter the electropositive vestibule, the fluoride ion at F0 is electrostatically repelled, providing energy for desolvation and translocation into the narrowest part of the channel at position F1.
source: We propose that as additional fluoride ions enter the electropositive vestibule, the fluoride ion at F0 is electrostatically repelled, providing energy for desolvation and translocation into the narrowest part of the channel at position F1 (Figure 5, right panel).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal illustrated in Figure 5.

claim: The F1 binding site is not pre-assembled: rotamerization of the vestibule serine (S83 in Fluc-Bpe) accompanies the lateral movement of the anion.
source: But the F1 binding site is not pre-assembled: rotamerization of the vestibule serine (S83 in Fluc-Bpe), which is possible with serine but not threonine, accompanies the lateral movement of the anion.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on structural and functional data.

claim: Other sidechains have been proposed to adopt new rotameric conformations in order to ligand the anion at F1, including N43 and S84.
source: Other sidechains have also been proposed to adopt new rotameric conformations in order to ligand the anion at F1, including N43 (Stockbridge et al., 2015) and S84 (Last et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a reference to previous mechanistic proposals.

claim: The F1 binding site is assembled simultaneously with its occupation by fluoride.
source: Thus, we propose that the F1 binding site is assembled simultaneously with its occupation by fluoride.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal based on the data and previous proposals.

claim: The rotamerization of channel sidechains to accompany ions through the pore has been proposed for other channels as well, including the Orai and voltage-gated calcium channels.
source: The rotamerization of channel sidechains to accompany ions through the pore has been proposed for other channels as well, including the Orai and voltage-gated calcium channels (Hou et al., 2020; Sather and McCleskey, 2003).
evidence: This is a reference to mechanistic proposals in other ion channels.

claim: A new fluoride ion settles into the deep vestibule F0 site, the fluoride at F1 moves farther down the channel to F2, and the S83 sidechain returns to its position facing the vestibule.
source: We imagine that this configuration is short-lived: a new fluoride ion settles into the deep vestibule F0 site, the fluoride at F1 moves farther down the channel to F2, and the S83 sidechain returns to its position facing the vestibule.
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal for the permeation cycle.

claim: The binding site at F2 is in close proximity to the E88 carboxylate; the electrostatic conflict could be resolved if E88 swings out into solution, allowing the fluoride at F2 to exit the channel.
source: The binding site at F2 is in close proximity to the E88 carboxylate; the electrostatic conflict could be resolved if E88 swings out into solution, allowing the fluoride at F2 to exit the channel, having now traversed the bilayer (whereby E88 could then resume its position at the pore exit without conflict).
evidence: This is a mechanistic proposal for fluoride exit.

claim: The E88Q mutant reduces both fluoride currents and block of fluoride currents by OCN- because the mutant sidechain, which does not bear a negative charge, is not easily dislodged from the binding site via electrostatic conflicts.
source: We have shown that the E88Q mutant reduces both fluoride currents and block of fluoride currents by OCN-. We propose that both behaviors arise because the mutant sidechain, which does not bear a negative charge, is not easily dislodged from the binding site via electrostatic conflicts with the permeant fluoride or the cyanate blocker.
evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the E88Q functional data.

claim: No mutant that permits the permeation of any other anion has been reported yet despite dozens of point mutations to two homologs.
source: Despite dozens of point mutations to two homologs, alone and in combination (summarized in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Table 4), no mutant that permits the permeation of any other anion has been reported yet.
evidence: This is a summary of the mutagenesis results.

claim: There may be no unique selectivity filter but several regions of the channel work together to achieve selectivity, so that abolishing anion selectivity requires destruction of the channel itself.
source: It may be that there is no unique selectivity filter but that several regions of the channel work together to achieve selectivity, so that abolishing anion selectivity requires destruction of the channel itself.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism of selectivity.

claim: Channel selectivity might be achieved by matching the number of available ligands in the pore to the preferred coordination number of the anion, as has been proposed for K+ channels.
source: Alternatively, channel selectivity might be achieved by matching the number of available ligands in the pore to the preferred coordination number of the anion, as has been proposed for K+ channels (Bostick and Brooks, 2007; Bostick and Brooks, 2009).
evidence: This is a speculation based on principles from K+ channel selectivity.

claim: F- requires fewer ligands than any other anion.
source: F- is a superlative in this regard, requiring fewer ligands than any other anion.
evidence: This is a chemical property of fluoride.

claim: The F1 and F2 sites have relatively small coordination numbers (~four including the phenylalanine ring edges).
source: Indeed, even accounting for the addition of coordinating ligands via sidechain rotamerization, the F1 and F2 sites have relatively small coordination numbers (~four including the phenylalanine ring edges).
evidence: This is a structural observation and inference.

claim: Chloride prefers at least six ligands in its coordination sphere.
source: Chloride, in contrast, prefers at least six ligands in its coordination sphere (Bostick and Brooks, 2009; Ohtaki and Radnai, 1993; Cametti and Rissanen, 2009; Merchant and Asthagiri, 2009).
evidence: This is a chemical property of chloride supported by citations.

claim: In the bacterial cytoplasm, during an F- challenge, F- ion is between 100 μM and 10 mM.
source: But in the bacterial cytoplasm, during an F- challenge, with F- ion between 100 μM and 10 mM (Ji et al., 2014), and Cl- ion between 10 and 100 mM (Schultz et al., 1962), even a small increase in the inhibitory effects of Cl- would represent a serious challenge to the efficacy of these channels and the survival of the bacteria.
evidence: This is a physiological context supported by citations.

claim: In the bacterial cytoplasm, Cl- ion is between 10 and 100 mM.
source: But in the bacterial cytoplasm, during an F- challenge, with F- ion between 100 μM and 10 mM (Ji et al., 2014), and Cl- ion between 10 and 100 mM (Schultz et al., 1962), even a small increase in the inhibitory effects of Cl- would represent a serious challenge to the efficacy of these channels and the survival of the bacteria.
evidence: This is a physiological context supported by citations.

claim: Even a small increase in the inhibitory effects of Cl- would represent a serious challenge to the efficacy of Fluc channels and the survival of the bacteria.
source: But in the bacterial cytoplasm, during an F- challenge, with F- ion between 100 μM and 10 mM (Ji et al., 2014), and Cl- ion between 10 and 100 mM (Schultz et al., 1962), even a small increase in the inhibitory effects of Cl- would represent a serious challenge to the efficacy of these channels and the survival of the bacteria.
evidence: This is a physiological interpretation of the selectivity data.
